newsitem.title: USA: Rubin opposes cutting ethanol fuel-tax break.
newsitem.headline: Rubin opposes cutting ethanol fuel-tax break.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin served notice on Thursday that the White House will fight Republican efforts to pare back and eventually wipe out a tax break for users of ethanol.

"The administration continues to support the ethanol credits as evidenced by the proposed extension of the excise credit...earlier this year," Rubin said in a one-sentence statement issued by Treasury.
House tax-writing chief Bill Archer said on Monday he wanted a slight cut -- 0.3 cent per gallon -- in the 5.4 cent fuel-tax break for ethanol and an end to the break in 2000.
Ethanol is made from corn. Archer maintains the existing tax break diverts corn to an artificial, industrial use when the world needs more food.
But the tax break has strong support among farm-state lawmakers and from backers of ethanol use who say it is a low-pollution fuel that supports 120,000 jobs for farmers and grain processors.
